title: Gaia wide binaries within 200 pc have a 6 percent low-acceleration velocity excess after hidden-companion flags, less than a 14 percent MOND-like boost; orbit-model choices change it by 5 percent
abstract: Question: Do Gaia wide binaries show a MOND-type velocity boost at low internal acceleration when hidden companions are removed with new flags? Method: We used 49,836 main-sequence pairs within 200 pc from the El-Badry et al. (2021) catalogue. We flagged hidden companions by the change in proper motion between Gaia DR2 and EDR3 (frame spin removed, errors calibrated), by IPD multi-peak data, and by a differential colour-magnitude offset between the two stars. A per-pair Newtonian Monte Carlo predicted the median normalized velocity v~. It includes each pair's errors, the perspective term, the measured separation slope, and an eccentricity index fitted in each bin from v-r angles. The pre-set statistic is delta = R(g_N < 3e-10)/R(g_N > 3e-9), where R is the observed median v~ divided by the Newtonian median. Newton gives 1. A MOND-like reference (simple nu with external field 1.9 a0) gives about 1.14. Mock catalogues recovered 1.00 and 1.17. Result: Flag-clean pairs give delta = 1.063 (95%: 1.003-1.134; n = 1,312 low and 5,233 high). RUWE-only pairs give 1.088 (1.040-1.139). Only 2% of bootstrap draws reach the MOND-like reference. Pairs with a DR2-EDR3 flag have median v~ 37-43% above Newton at all accelerations; thus RUWE < 1.2 samples keep fast pairs with companions. In 11 clean variants, delta is 0.98-1.10 and always below the reference. A constant separation-slope prior removes the excess, and a fixed eccentricity index raises delta to 1.09-1.10. The colour-magnitude companion rate increases from 29% at 200-500 au to 38-41% beyond 500 au. Limitation: One mass-luminosity relation, only DR2 radial velocities, a median test without an explicit triple model, and an approximate MOND reference. The residual excess cannot be separated from residual contamination.

display.caption: a) Observed median v~ divided by the Newtonian prediction, relative to g_N > 3e-9 m/s^2, in six acceleration bins. Blue: flag-clean pairs. Grey: RUWE < 1.2 only. Purple: pairs with any hidden-companion flag set. Red dashed: MOND-like reference. Error bars: 68% bootstrap. b) Eccentricity index alpha fitted to v-r angles in each bin.

Pre-set statistic delta = R(g_N < 3e-10)/R(g_N > 3e-9) for all samples and analysis variants (68% thick, 95% thin bootstrap intervals). Newton = 1. Red crosses: MOND-like reference for the same pairs.

Hidden-companion flag rates against projected separation (angle > 4 arcsec) and against angular separation: RUWE > 1.2, DR2->EDR3 proper-motion change (p < 0.001), IPD multi-peak or GoF harmonic, and differential colour-magnitude offset > 0.3 mag (pairs with valid colours).

citations.reason: Wide-binary catalogue (Gaia EDR3 with DR2 cross-match) used as the input sample.
Zenodo record of the El-Badry et al. 2021 catalogue (CC BY 4.0).
Chae 2023 reports a MOND-type gravitational anomaly in Gaia wide binaries; our flag-clean median test finds a smaller excess.
Chae and Yoon 2026 report a gravity boost of 1.3-1.6; our delta is below a 1.38 MOND-like reference.
Chae et al. 2026 3D test with 36 binaries reports gamma = 1.6.
Banik et al. 2024 find Newtonian gravity and emphasize hidden triples; our DR2-EDR3 flags show fast companion-hosting pairs in RUWE-cut samples.
Saad and Ting 2026 find gamma consistent with 1 and show sensitivity to orbit modelling, which agrees with our variant spread.
Pittordis, Sutherland and Shepherd 2025 triple modelling in Gaia DR3 wide binaries.
Hernandez et al. critical review of wide-binary gravity tests.
v-r angle method for eccentricity distributions (Hwang, Ting and Zakamska 2022).
Corrected BP/RP excess factor C* used to select valid colours (Riello et al. 2021).
Pecaut and Mamajek 2013 / Mamajek table 2022.04.16 used for the M_G to mass relation.
